Canadian Mayor Wants His Co-op to Be An Official Supplier of Medical Marijuana

MAYOR WANTS TO CORNER MARIJUANA MARKET

See
Canadian Health Minister Issues Call To All Pot Growers To Send Him Their Resumes.
In The Meantime, He Is Going To Try To Get Marijuana From DEAland.
Maybe He Will Have Better Luck Than Our Own Researchers.
Two AIDS Patients Get Exemptions.
June 14, 1999
From The Vancouver Province
provletters@pacpress.southam.ca
http://www.vancouverprovince.com/
By Ian Austin - Staff Reporter

Grand Forks Mayor Brian Taylor wants to be Canada’s official supplier of marijuana.

Taylor, an outspoken pot advocate who’s been banned from entering the U.S. for his views, sees a potential gold mine now that the Canadian government has approved clinical trials of medical marijuana.

"It could be a billion-dollar industry in Canada," said Taylor, who lives next to the U.S. border but can’t cross it.

See

"Our community is looking for a clean, green industry. Eighty-three per cent of Canadians support medical marijuana and our community’s no different."
See
78 Percent Of Canadians Favor Medical Marijuana – What Is Rock Waiting On? DEAland?

Taylor has reason to believe the Canadian contract - or at least part of it - could soon be his. Brown Bear Medicinals, a co-op run by Taylor and a dozen others, was accepted as an official bidder by the National Institute on Drug Addiction.

"They supply Mississippi and the eight approved marijuana users in the United States," said Taylor, who’s in his third year as mayor. "They’re looking for a safe, reliable source povided in a secure environment and we say we can deliver the goods in 120 days."
